name: dead-store-around-a-closure
description: In Go a function literal reads each variable it names where it is written, and a store that a literal naming its variable may precede on some path of the control-flow graph, a literal of an earlier iteration of a loop included, is not dead, because a call of the literal the graph does not order may read it. A store no such literal precedes is judged as any other, so a store overwritten before the literal is written is dead. A literal called where it is written, outside a go or defer statement, runs there, so a store after the call is judged as any other, while one a goroutine's literal precedes is not dead.
